doc.title: Billie Pierce, De De Pierce, Israel Gorman, Joseph "Kid Twat" Butler Interview, 1963-11-20

title: Learning the Creole song Hey La Ba
summary: He says he learned the song from Creole-speaking elders and added words, not from a band.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Oh, I see. Well, how did you learn this number, Hey, La, Ba?

Well, the pastor and I, of course, most of the men spoke Creole. Father Tim said, Hey, La, Ba. Hey, La, Ba. And just wanted to know a thing. Thought about it. And got up and sang. Put adding words, adding words to it. That's how I got started.
Oh, I see. And who did you learn this number the time you drew your apron strings again? Well, from the music.
Most of the music. You didn't hear? I brought the music in the words, you know. Oh. I just remember, you know.
You didn't hear a special band around town featured?
I thought maybe Fate featured that or something about it.
I've heard a lot of bands play there, too. Oh, I see. Yeah, I played with them.
